Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 40-year-old woman with three-week history of progressive left-sided hearing loss, constant numbness along left jaw/ear, intermittent left-sided tinnitus, and occasional dizziness. No otalgia, discharge, fever, limb weakness, dysphasia, or visual change.  
- Differential considerations:  
  • Idiopathic facial-nerve neuritis (Bell’s palsy) – discussed by clinician; will be assessed for facial nerve involvement.  
  • Vestibular schwannoma – compatible with unilateral sensorineural symptoms and family history of neurofibromatosis; warrants exclusion with targeted examination and possible imaging (derived from DDx; aligns with transcript features).  
  • Ramsay Hunt syndrome and other less-likely causes (from DDx) considered but no pain or rash.  
- Plan from video visit: Arrange face-to-face appointment today for full neurological exam and otoscopy to confirm or refute Bell’s palsy and to evaluate other causes. Reassured patient condition unlikely life-threatening but requires same-day assessment.

Management Plan
- Same-day in-person GP clinic appointment booked via support team for complete cranial-nerve exam and ear examination.  
- Provide contact number and instructions for booking.  
- Further management (e.g., imaging, ENT referral, corticosteroids) to be determined after physical examination.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) – High likelihood: unilateral progressive hearing loss, tinnitus, facial numbness, family history of neurofibromatosis.  
2. Idiopathic facial-nerve neuritis (Bell’s palsy) – Moderate likelihood: unilateral facial sensory symptoms; clinician’s working diagnosis though sensory > motor signs make it less typical.  
3. Ramsay Hunt syndrome – Low-moderate likelihood: could explain symptoms but lacks pain or vesicular rash.
